sentences.cn_text: 英国金融监管机构对大型银行的负责人施加了一项相当不同寻常的规定。
sentences.en_text: Financial regulators in Britain have imposed a rather unusual rule on the bosses of big banks.

sentences.cn_text: 从明年开始,如果银行因不当行为受到调查,高管的保证奖金可能会被延迟10年发放。
sentences.en_text: Starting next year, any guaranteed bonus of top executives could be delayed 10 years if their banks are under investigation for wrongdoing.

sentences.cn_text: 这一「追回」规则的主要目的是让银行家为有害的冒险行为负责,并恢复公众对金融机构的信任。
sentences.en_text: The main purpose of this “clawback” rule is to hold bankers accountable for harmful risk-taking and to restore public trust in financial institutions.

sentences.cn_text: 然而,官员们也期待获得更大的收益:不仅银行,所有公司都能做出更多长期决策,以为子孙后代构建更强大的经济。
sentences.en_text: Yet officials also hope for a much larger benefit: more long-term decisionmaking, not only by banks but by all corporations, to build a stronger economy for future generations.

sentences.cn_text: 英国央行首席经济学家安德鲁·霍尔丹表示,「短期主义」或对快速利润的追求,在上市公司中愈演愈烈。
sentences.en_text: “Short-termism” or the desire for quick profits, has worsened in publicly traded companies, says the Bank of England’s top economist, Andrew Haldane.

sentences.cn_text: 他引用古典经济学巨擘阿尔弗雷德·马歇尔的话,将这种金融上的急功近利比作「孩子们从布丁里挑出李子立刻吃掉」,而不是留到最后再吃。
sentences.en_text: He quotes a giant of classical economics, Alfred Marshall, in describing this financial impatience as acting like “children who pick the plums out of their pudding to eat them at once” rather than putting them aside to be eaten last.

sentences.cn_text: 他指出,近几十年来,美国和英国的股票持有平均时长已从七年降至七个月。
sentences.en_text: The average time for holding a stock in both the United States and Britain, he notes, has dropped from seven years to seven months in recent decades.

sentences.cn_text: 要求公司实现高季度利润的短期投资者,可能会妨碍企业在长期研发或建立客户忠诚度方面的投入。
sentences.en_text: Transient investors, who demand high quarterly profits from companies, can hinder a firm’s efforts to invest in longterm research or to build up customer loyalty.

sentences.cn_text: 这被称为「季度资本主义」。
sentences.en_text: This has been dubbed “quarterly capitalism.”

sentences.cn_text: 此外,新兴数字技术使股票交易更加迅速,信息利用更加快捷,从而缩短了金融市场的注意力持续时间。
sentences.en_text: In addition, new digital technologies have allowed more rapid trading of equities, quicker use of information, and thus shorter attention spans in financial markets.

sentences.cn_text: 美国证券交易委员会委员丹尼尔·加拉格在本周的一次演讲中表示:「短期思维似乎占据主导地位,而长期投资却被牺牲了。」
sentences.en_text: “There seems to be a predominance of short-term thinking at the expense of long-term investing,” said Commissioner Daniel Gallagher of the US Securities and Exchange Commission in a speech this week.

sentences.cn_text: 在美国,2002年的《萨班斯-奥克斯利法案》促使大多数上市公司将高管绩效奖金推迟约一年发放,在一定程度上有助于减少「短期主义」。《华尔街日报》在其最新的CEO薪酬调查中发现,「相当大比例」的高管薪酬现已与绩效挂钩。
sentences.en_text: In the US, the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 has pushed most public companies to defer performance bonuses for senior executives by about a year, slightly helping reduce “shorttermism.” In its latest survey of CEO pay, The Wall Street Journal finds that “a substantial part” of executive pay is now tied to performance.

sentences.cn_text: 可以采取更多措施来鼓励「长期主义」,例如修改税法和加快股票收购信息的披露。
sentences.en_text: Much more could be done to encourage “long-termism,” such as changes in the tax code and quicker disclosure of stock acquisitions.

sentences.cn_text: 在法国,持有公司股权至少两年的股东有时可以获得更多投票权。
sentences.en_text: In France, shareholders who hold onto a company investment for at least two years can sometimes earn more voting rights in a company.

sentences.cn_text: 在公司内部,合理的薪酬设计可以激励高管超越自身任期考虑问题,并代表所有利益相关者行事。
sentences.en_text: Within companies, the right compensation design can provide incentives for executives to think beyond their own time at the company and on behalf of all stakeholders.

sentences.cn_text: 英国的新规提醒银行家,社会关注的不仅是他们的短期表现,也包括长期表现。
sentences.en_text: Britain’s new rule is a reminder to bankers that society has an interest in their performance, not just for the short term but for the long term.
